```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"

```

Copy-pasted numbers in research manuscripts routinely drift out of sync with fitted R models during peer review, sample filtering, or covariate revisions. `statci` verifies prose statistics, Markdown/Quarto tables, LaTeX `.tex` manuscripts, and internal statistical arithmetic directly against saved model objects.

```{r setup}
library(statci)
```

## 1. Auditing Prose and Markdown/Quarto Tables Together

`audit_manuscript()` parses both inline APA prose (`b`, `SE`, `t(df)`, `F(df1, df2)`, `chi2(df)`, `95% CI`, `p`, `OR`, `r`, `R^2`, `N`, `AIC`, `BIC`) and Markdown/Quarto pipe tables:

```{r qmd-table-demo}
fit_mpg <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)

qmd_path <- system.file("examples", "sample-manuscript.qmd", package = "statci")
if (nzchar(qmd_path)) {
  res_qmd <- audit_manuscript(qmd_path, models = list(primary = fit_mpg))
  res_qmd
  as_tibble(res_qmd)[, c("line", "term", "metric", "reported_raw", "actual", "issue_type", "status")]
}
```

## 2. Catching Sign Flips, Rounding Discrepancies, Table Drift & Stale Sample Sizes

Consider a manuscript where an author updated the model after dropping outliers, but forgot to update a sign in prose, entered a stale table cell, and left the old sample size `N = 40`:

```{r catch-drift}
drifted_md <- paste(
  "<!-- statci: model=primary term=wt -->",
  "Vehicle weight positively predicted MPG (*b* = 5.34, SE = 0.56, *p* < .001, *N* = 40).",
  "",
  "<!-- statci: model=primary -->",
  "| Term | b | SE | t | 95% CI | p |",
  "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
  "| wt | -5.33 | 0.56 | -9.56 | [-6.49, -4.20] | < .001 |",
  sep = "\n"
)

drift_res <- audit_manuscript_text(drifted_md, models = list(primary = fit_mpg))
drift_res
as_tibble(drift_res)[, c("line", "metric", "reported_raw", "actual", "issue_type", "status")]
```

Notice how `statci` distinguishes:
- **`sign_flip` (`fail`)**: `b = 5.34` vs actual `-5.3445`
- **`stale_sample_size` (`fail`)**: `N = 40` vs actual `32`
- **`rounding_discrepancy` (`warn`)**: table cell `-5.33` is off by 0.01 in the final decimal place relative to `-5.3445`.

## 3. Auditing APA F-Statistics, Chi-Squared Tests & Scientific Notation

`audit_manuscript()` handles `F(df1, df2) = ...`, `chi2(df) = ...` (including `\chi^2`), odds ratios (`OR`), Unicode minus signs, leading-dot decimals (`-.42`, `.003`), and scientific notation (`1.2e-4`, `1.2 \times 10^{-4}`):

```{r apa-extras}
ct_mat <- matrix(c(30, 10, 12, 28), nrow = 2)
chi_fit <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(ct_mat, correct = FALSE))
chi_val <- formatC(as.numeric(chi_fit$statistic), digits = 2, format = "f")

apa_txt <- paste0(
  "<!-- statci: model=lm_fit -->\n",
  "Overall regression was significant, F(1, 30) = 91.38, R^2 = 0.75, N = 32.\n",
  "<!-- statci: model=chi_fit -->\n",
  "Group proportions differed strongly, chi2(1) = ", chi_val, ", p < 1e-4."
)

audit_manuscript_text(apa_txt, models = list(lm_fit = fit_mpg, chi_fit = chi_fit))
```

## 4. Auditing LaTeX (`.tex`) Manuscripts and `tabular` Environments

For journal submissions written in LaTeX, `audit_manuscript()` natively strips `%` comments and `verbatim` blocks, unwraps `\textit`/`\mathrm`/`\beta`/`\chi^2`, recognizes `% statci:` comment anchors, and audits `\begin{tabular}...\end{tabular}` rows:

```{r tex-demo}
tex_path <- system.file("examples", "sample-manuscript.tex", package = "statci")
if (nzchar(tex_path)) {
  res_tex <- audit_manuscript(tex_path, models = list(primary = fit_mpg))
  res_tex
}
```

## 5. Standalone Internal Arithmetic Cross-Checking (Even Without Saved Models)

Even when no `.rds` model object is attached (`models = NULL`), `audit_manuscript_text(..., check_internal = TRUE)` uses **interval arithmetic** over rounding half-units to verify that reported `t`/`z` matches `b / SE` and that `95% CI` bounds are symmetric around `b` and consistent with `SE`:

```{r internal-arithmetic}
# Consistent clause passes
ok_arith <- audit_manuscript_text(
  "Effect of x: b = 0.42, SE = 0.11, t(98) = 3.82, 95% CI [0.20, 0.64].",
  models = NULL
)
ok_arith
ok_arith$internal_checks[, c("check_type", "reported_expr", "status", "detail")]

# Copy-paste typo (t = 1.15 instead of 3.82; CI shifted right) fails automatically
bad_arith <- audit_manuscript_text(
  "Effect of x: b = 0.42, SE = 0.11, t(98) = 1.15, 95% CI [0.40, 0.90].",
  models = NULL
)
bad_arith
bad_arith$internal_checks[, c("check_type", "status", "detail")]
```
